gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, at a TV-sized 50 W AC load, techtest.org measured only 366 Wh (71.5% of 512 Wh) from the EcoFlow RIVER 2 Max and 623 Wh (81% of 768 Wh) from the BLUETTI AC70. Both are below the 85% usable energy ChatGPT's runtime calculator assumes. The Technology Man also measured about 17 W of inverter draw on an Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 with AC on and nothing plugged in.
standout_why: I checked three pages. The cited bluettipower.com AC70 page gives only maker runtimes ('TV(65W): 8.2 Hours') and no efficiency, idle or third-party figure. powerstationsize.com/stations lists nameplate Wh and W only, with 'Specifications taken from manufacturer pages' and no tester named. The EcoFlow FAQ and manual PDFs ChatGPT got are maker documents. None of these pages has a measured low-load AC output figure or a measured idle draw for any of the three candidates. ChatGPT's 85% figure is its own assumption, not a source.
decides: It confirms that ChatGPT's capacity tiers point the right way, but its runtimes are too high at TV-level loads. A TV draws 50–100 W, which is where these inverters are least efficient. On techtest's 50 W numbers, a 50 W TV runs about 7.3 h on the RIVER 2 Max (366/50). That is below ChatGPT's own '8–14 hours' row for a 32-inch on a 500 Wh unit. The AC70 gives about 12.5 h (623/50). Measured usable energy per rated Wh favors the AC70 over the RIVER 2 Max for TV use. The C1000 Gen 2's roughly 17 W idle draw means a shopper watching TV in short sessions should switch AC off between sessions. One caveat: techtest and The Technology Man tested EU/UK 230–240 V units, and US 120 V inverters may measure differently.
